title: Arguing a position
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

allowedPatterns: Na pérvyy vzglyad + <clause> + , + no na sámom déle + <clause>

rules.text: THE CONCESSION-REFUTATION PAIR is one sentence in two halves: Na pervyy vzglyad … , no na samom dele … . The first half states the view you are about to answer, accurately and without irony; the second half answers it. Russian argues this way in print and in public the way English does, and getting the halves in this order is most of what makes a case sound argued rather than asserted.

THE BOOKISH CONNECTORS govern nothing. sledovatel'no (therefore), takim obrazom (thus), poskol'ku (since), vsledstviye and v rezul'tate (as a result), odnako (however), tem ne meneye (nevertheless) take no case and change no ending. All they cost is a comma — L3-M3's comma, which Russian sets before a subordinate clause and around an inserted connector. The whole teaching load here is register and slot, not grammar.

REGISTER, not meaning, is where English misleads. Each of these connectors has a spoken twin the learner already owns: sledovatel'no is the written form of znachit (L4-M2), poskol'ku of potomu chto (L1-M9) and tak kak (L4-M2), v rezul'tate of poetomu (L1-M9). Saying sledovatel'no over dinner is as odd as saying hence. The spoken ones are not weaker or lazier — they are the right word in the right room.

odnako is the one connector here with a second, spoken life: standing alone it is an exclamation of surprise, Odnako! — well I never. That is not a formal use and it is not an argument connector; it is the same word doing a different job, and it is named here rather than hidden because a learner will hear it.

TWO WRITTEN VARIANTS of things the learner already has. dlya togo chtoby is the heavy form of L4-M1's chtoby purpose clause — same meaning, printed register, and the three words are one frozen phrase. v techeniye plus the GENITIVE is the bookish duration phrase (v techeniye dnya, v techeniye nedeli). Each is shown beside the plain form it varies, never instead of it.

sentences.display: Na pérvyy vzglyad éhto prósto, no na sámom déle éhto trúdno.
sentences.script: На первый взгляд это просто, но на самом деле это трудно.
sentences.cue: At first glance it's simple, but in fact it's hard.
sentences.literal: At first glance this simple, but at very deed this hard.

words.note: At first glance. One frozen three-word phrase, so it is indexed whole; the bare ordinal pérvyy is not what this row teaches.
In fact. The second half of the concession pair, and a frozen phrase: literally in the very deed. It answers the view na pérvyy vzglyad just stated.
Hard, difficult — an impersonal adverb, so it needs no subject: Éhto trúdno, or just Trúdno.

sentences.trap: English drops actually anywhere in a sentence. na sámom déle is the back half of a pair and wants na pérvyy vzglyad standing in front of it.
sentences.sound: na pérvyy vzglyad runs together as na-PYER-vyy VZGLYAT, with the final d said as t. na sámom déle is na SA-mom DYE-lye.

variations.cue: At first glance it's simple.
variations.changed: the concession alone, with the refutation left unsaid

variations.cue: In fact it's hard.
variations.changed: the refutation alone, which lands as blunt without the concession

mistake.display: Na sámom déle éhto prósto, no na pérvyy vzglyad éhto trúdno.
mistake.script: На самом деле это просто, но на первый взгляд это трудно.
mistake.why: the halves swapped. na pérvyy vzglyad states the view you are about to answer, so it comes first; reversed, the sentence argues against itself.

sentences.usage: Written or public argument: state the opposing view fairly, then answer it.
sentences.mnemonic: First the glance, then the truth: na pérvyy vzglyad … no na sámom déle …

sentences.display: Mózhno vozrazít', chto éhto slíshkom dórogo.
sentences.script: Можно возразить, что это слишком дорого.
sentences.cue: One could object that it's too expensive.
sentences.literal: Possible to-object, that this too expensive.

words.note: One could object. L2-M1's mózhno plus the verb to object, taken whole because the pair is the frame; it always continues with chto.
Too, in the excessive sense: slíshkom dórogo is too expensive. Not the too that means also, which is tózhe.

sentences.trap: English one might argue can stand without a that-clause. mózhno vozrazít' cannot: drop the chto and the phrase reads as objecting to the thing itself.
sentences.sound: vozrazít' is va-zra-ZEET', stressed on the last syllable, with a soft final t.

variations.cue: One could object that it's hard.
variations.changed: a different objection inside the same frame

variations.cue: It's too expensive.
variations.changed: the objection bare, without the frame that introduces it

mistake.why: the chto dropped. mózhno vozrazít' takes a chto-clause; without it, éhto reads as the thing being objected to rather than as the objection.

sentences.usage: Answering the strongest objection before anyone in the room makes it.
sentences.mnemonic: mózhno vozrazít' always takes chto — one may object THAT.

sentences.display: Poskól'ku éhto vázhno, my dolzhný rabótat' závtra.
sentences.script: Поскольку это важно, мы должны работать завтра.
sentences.cue: Since this is important, we have to work tomorrow.
sentences.literal: Since this important, we must to-work tomorrow.

words.note: Since, in the reasoning sense. The written twin of tak kak, and like it it fronts the sentence comfortably: Poskól'ku …, … .

sentences.trap: English since is also a time word (since Monday). Russian poskól'ku is only the reasoning one; the time sense is s plus the genitive.
sentences.sound: poskól'ku is pas-KOL'-ku. The soft sign after the l is the whole difference from a hard l.

variations.cue: Since it was important, we worked.
variations.changed: the same reason with a past-tense result

variations.cue: Since it's hard, time is needed.
variations.changed: an impersonal main clause after the same connector

mistake.display: Poskól'ku éhto vázhno my dolzhný rabótat' závtra.
mistake.script: Поскольку это важно мы должны работать завтра.
mistake.why: the comma gone. A fronted poskól'ku clause closes with a comma before the main clause, exactly as L3-M3 sets it.

sentences.usage: Written reasoning. In speech a Russian reaches for potomú chto or tak kak instead.
sentences.mnemonic: poskól'ku is tak kak in a suit: same meaning, printed page.

sentences.display: Ya rabótal ves' den', slédovatel'no, ya ustál.
sentences.script: Я работал весь день, следовательно, я устал.
sentences.cue: I worked all day, therefore I'm tired.
sentences.literal: I worked all day, consequently, I tired.

words.note: The whole of a single thing: ves' den' is all day. Different from vsyó, which is everything, and from vsé, which is everybody.
Therefore. Front-stressed, and it sits between commas. Its spoken twin is znáchit, which is what a Russian actually says in a kitchen.

sentences.trap: English therefore can sit at the head with no comma behind it. slédovatel'no is an inserted word and takes a comma on both sides.
sentences.sound: slédovatel'no is FRONT-stressed: SLYE-da-va-tyel'-na. Learners regularly say slyeda-VA-tyel'no, and that is wrong.

variations.cue: I worked all day.
variations.changed: the premise on its own

variations.display: Ya ustál, slédovatel'no, ya ne rabótayu.
variations.script: Я устал, следовательно, я не работаю.
variations.cue: I'm tired, therefore I'm not working.
variations.changed: the same connector with the conclusion in the present

mistake.display: Ya rabótal ves' den', poéhtomu slédovatel'no ya ustál.
mistake.script: Я работал весь день, поэтому следовательно я устал.
mistake.why: two connectors for one join. poéhtomu and slédovatel'no do the same job in different registers; pick one, and pick it by the room you are in.

sentences.usage: The written case, where the conclusion is drawn out loud from the premise.
sentences.mnemonic: slédovatel'no is znáchit with its shoes on — same step, better shoes.

sentences.display: Tem ne méneye, ya s vámi ne soglásen.
sentences.script: Тем не менее, я с вами не согласен.
sentences.cue: Nevertheless, I don't agree with you.
sentences.literal: By-that not less, I with you not agreeing.

words.note: Nevertheless. Three words said as one; the ne inside is part of the phrase and negates nothing in the clause after it.

sentences.trap: The ne inside tem ne méneye belongs to the phrase and negates nothing after it. The clause still needs its own ne, as this one has.
sentences.sound: tem ne méneye is tyem nye MYE-nye-ye, said in one breath with the stress on the third word.

variations.cue: Nevertheless, it's important.
variations.changed: a short main clause after the same connector

variations.cue: I don't agree with you.
variations.changed: the disagreement without the concession in front of it

mistake.display: Ne méneye, ya s vámi ne soglásen.
mistake.script: Не менее, я с вами не согласен.
mistake.why: tem dropped. The phrase is three words and none of them is optional; ne méneye alone means no less and is not a connector at all.

sentences.usage: Conceding a point and then holding your ground anyway, in writing or in public.
sentences.mnemonic: Three words, one connector: tem ne méneye is nevertheless, never not less.

sentences.display: Takím óbrazom, otsyúda sléduyet odín právil'nyy vývod.
sentences.script: Таким образом, отсюда следует один правильный вывод.
sentences.cue: Thus, one correct conclusion follows from this.
sentences.literal: Such way, from-here follows one correct conclusion.

words.note: Thus, in this way. Frozen in the instrumental, so neither word changes; it opens the sentence that draws the conclusion.
It follows. Impersonal, so the conclusion is its subject: Otsyúda sléduyet odín vývod — one conclusion follows from this.
Correct, of a thing rather than a person. A person who is right is prav, which is L3-M3's.
A conclusion, the thing an argument arrives at. Front-stressed: VÝ-vod.

sentences.trap: English says the conclusion is that …; Russian makes the conclusion the SUBJECT of sléduyet, so the verb agrees with vývod and not with the arguer.
sentences.sound: óbrazom is O-bra-zam, front-stressed. sléduyet is SLYE-du-yet, and vývod is VÝ-vod.

variations.cue: One conclusion follows from this.
variations.changed: the conclusion without the connector

variations.cue: Thus, that's the right conclusion.
variations.changed: the connector with a plain naming clause instead

mistake.display: Takím óbrazom, otsyúda sléduyut odín právil'nyy vývod.
mistake.script: Таким образом, отсюда следуют один правильный вывод.
mistake.why: a plural verb under a singular subject. One vývod follows, so the verb is sléduyet; sléduyut would need vývody standing there.

sentences.usage: Closing a written case: the sentence that names what has been shown.
sentences.mnemonic: takím óbrazom points forward at the vývod, and sléduyet agrees with it.

sentences.display: Vslédstviye dozhdyá my rabótali dóma v techéniye dnya.
sentences.script: Вследствие дождя мы работали дома в течение дня.
sentences.cue: Because of the rain we worked at home all day long.
sentences.literal: In-consequence of-rain we worked at-home in course of-day.

words.note: As a result of, and it takes the GENITIVE: vslédstviye dozhdyá. Stressed on the second syllable, not the first.
Over the course of, plus the GENITIVE: v techéniye dnya. The bookish duration phrase beside L4-M6's plain accusative of time.

sentences.trap: English because of and during both take a plain noun. Both of these take the GENITIVE, so dozhd' becomes dozhdyá and den' becomes dnya.
sentences.sound: vslédstviye is stressed on its SECOND syllable, vslyed-STVI-ye. techéniye is tye-CHE-ni-ye.

variations.cue: Because of the rain we worked at home.
variations.changed: the cause without the duration

variations.display: My rabótali dóma v techéniye dnya.
variations.script: Мы работали дома в течение дня.
variations.cue: We worked at home all day long.
variations.changed: the duration without the cause

mistake.why: the dictionary form left standing. vslédstviye governs the genitive, so it is vslédstviye dozhdyá — the same ending L4-M2's iz-za takes.

sentences.usage: Reports, minutes, notices — the register that explains why something did not happen.
sentences.mnemonic: Both of these prepositions eat a genitive: vslédstviye dozhdyá, v techéniye dnya.

sentences.display: Bezuslóvno, v rezul'táte vsyó býlo khoroshó.
sentences.script: Безусловно, в результате всё было хорошо.
sentences.cue: Certainly, in the end everything was fine.
sentences.literal: Undoubtedly, in result all was well.

words.note: As a result. Stands alone as a connector, unlike vslédstviye, which always wants a genitive noun behind it.
Certainly, undoubtedly. It concedes a point wholeheartedly, which is what makes the no that follows land.

sentences.trap: English certainly can be a grudging half-concession. bezuslóvno is not grudging: it grants the point completely, which is exactly what makes a following no land hard.
sentences.sound: bezuslóvno is bye-zoos-LOV-na. rezul'táte is rye-zool'-TA-tye.

variations.cue: In the end everything was fine.
variations.changed: the result without the concession

variations.cue: Certainly, that's important.
variations.changed: the concession on its own, granting the other side its point

mistake.display: Bezuslóvno, v rezul'tát vsyó býlo khoroshó.
mistake.script: Безусловно, в результат всё было хорошо.
mistake.why: the accusative under a static v. v rezul'táte is the prepositional and describes where things ended up, not motion into a result.

sentences.usage: Granting the other side its strongest point before answering it.
sentences.mnemonic: bezuslóvno concedes everything, so the sentence after it has to earn its no.

sentences.display: Odnáko deystvítel'no trúdno rabótat' ves' den'.
sentences.script: Однако действительно трудно работать весь день.
sentences.cue: However, it really is hard to work all day.
sentences.literal: However really hard to-work all day.

words.note: However. It can open the clause or sit inside it between commas; standing alone it is a spoken cry of surprise instead.
Really, indeed — it grants that something is so. Stressed on the third syllable: deyst-VI-tyel'-na.

sentences.trap: English however is only a connector. odnáko is that too, but standing alone with an exclamation mark it is a spoken cry of surprise — the same word, a different job.
sentences.sound: odnáko is ad-NA-ka, stressed in the middle. deystvítel'no is deyst-VI-tyel'-na.

variations.cue: However, it's hard.
variations.changed: the connector with the shortest possible clause

variations.cue: Indeed, it really is too expensive.
variations.changed: the concession adverb granting the other side its fact

mistake.display: No odnáko trúdno rabótat' ves' den'.
mistake.script: Но однако трудно работать весь день.
mistake.why: no and odnáko are the same however said twice. Russian takes one of them per clause, and odnáko is the written one.

sentences.usage: Turning the case after a concession, in the register of a printed argument.
sentences.mnemonic: odnáko is the printed no; Odnáko! on its own is a raised eyebrow.

sentences.display: Naprótiv, dlya tovó chtóby rabótat' khoroshó, núzhno vrémya.
sentences.script: Напротив, для того чтобы работать хорошо, нужно время.
sentences.cue: On the contrary, in order to work well one needs time.
sentences.literal: On-the-contrary, for that in-order-to to-work well, necessary time.

words.note: On the contrary. It does not merely disagree, it asserts the opposite, so what follows must be the opposite claim.
In order to — the heavy written form of L4-M1's plain chtóby. Three words, one phrase, and the middle word is the genitive of that.

sentences.trap: English on the contrary is often only a softer however. naprótiv asserts the OPPOSITE, so what follows it must actually be the opposite claim, not a milder one.
sentences.sound: naprótiv is na-PRO-tif, with the final v said as f. dlya tovó chtóby is dlya ta-VO SHTO-by.

variations.display: Dlya tovó chtóby rabótat' khoroshó, núzhno vrémya.
variations.script: Для того чтобы работать хорошо, нужно время.
variations.cue: In order to work well, one needs time.
variations.changed: the purpose clause without the contrary turn

variations.cue: On the contrary, it's very simple.
variations.changed: the contrary turn with the shortest opposite claim

mistake.display: Naprótiv, dlya chtóby rabótat' khoroshó, núzhno vrémya.
mistake.script: Напротив, для чтобы работать хорошо, нужно время.
mistake.why: tovó dropped out of the middle. The written purpose phrase is all three words, dlya tovó chtóby; the plain form is chtóby alone, with no dlya in front of it.

sentences.usage: A written rebuttal that replaces the other side's claim rather than softening it.
sentences.mnemonic: naprótiv promises the opposite; dlya tovó chtóby is chtóby in its Sunday clothes.

comprehensionPool.cue: One could object that it's expensive.
Since there's no time, I'm working.

comprehensionPool.display: Ya ustál, slédovatel'no, ya ne rabótayu.
comprehensionPool.script: Я устал, следовательно, я не работаю.
comprehensionPool.cue: I'm tired, therefore I'm not working.

comprehensionPool.display: Tem ne méneye, ya ne soglásen.
comprehensionPool.script: Тем не менее, я не согласен.

comprehensionPool.cue: In the end everything was fine.
Because of the rain we worked at home.

comprehensionPool.display: Dlya tovó chtóby rabótat', núzhno vrémya.
comprehensionPool.script: Для того чтобы работать, нужно время.
comprehensionPool.cue: In order to work, one needs time.
